entities.summary:
Gaius Furnius was a Roman senator during the reign of Augustus, and consul in 17 BC with Gaius Junius Silanus as his colleague.

As consul, Furnius played a crucial role in the governance of Rome, particularly in the administration of the provinces.

His legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Roman Empire on modern Western society, with many of its institutions, laws, and cultural practices still in use today.

The Roman historian Tacitus described Furnius as a man of 'exemplary integrity' and ' unwavering dedication to the Republic'.

Furnius's contributions to Roman history were also marked by his involvement in the construction of several public buildings, including the Temple of Apollo in Rome.

In the centuries following his death, Furnius's name became associated with the concept of 'Romanitas', or Roman identity, which continues to shape Western culture and politics to this day.

The impact of Furnius's actions can be seen in the many modern-day institutions and traditions that owe their origins to the Roman Empire.

Furnius's legacy serves as a reminder of the enduring power of Roman civilization and its lasting impact on the modern world.
